# Benchmarks

Measured 2026-11-09. These are numbers from one machine, not guarantees.

**Hardware and conditions:**

- Intel Core i7-12700 · 64 GB RAM · NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070.
- Windows 11 Pro (build 26300) · WebView2 157.
- Window 1280×800 CSS px at DPR 1, on a 3440×1440 display.
- Release build (`pnpm tauri build`, LTO).
- Other desktop applications open; no isolation.

**Maps:** generated by `crates/map-core/examples/bench.rs`. Nodes sit on a grid;
each links to the next node and to the node below, so edges = 2 × nodes. Every
fifth edge is labeled.

## Engine (Rust, median of 15 runs)

`cargo run --release -p map-core --example bench -- target/bench`

| nodes | edges | file KB | parse+validate ms | save ms (atomic, fsync) | SVG export ms | 100-node move tx + undo ms |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 200 | 53 | 0.49 | 2.42 | 0.60 | 0.21 |
| 500 | 1000 | 269 | 2.85 | 3.32 | 3.24 | 0.51 |
| 1000 | 2000 | 541 | 6.51 | 5.85 | 8.11 | 0.96 |

## Desktop app (Playwright over WebView2 DevTools)

`VUECRAFT_EXE=target/release/vuecraft.exe VUECRAFT_BENCH_DIR=target/bench pnpm test:e2e:playwright-legacy bench`
(legacy Playwright suite, outside the gates)

| nodes | open → all nodes rendered ms | 60-step node drag ms | frame gap p95 / max ms during drag | 20 wheel zoom events ms | Export SVG ms (IPC + write) | JS heap MB | Rust host working set MB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 66 | 1020 | 16.8 / 16.8 | 687 | 8 | 38.3 | 27.6 |
| 500 | 213 | 2282 | 16.8 / 16.9 | 725 | 10 | 83.2 | 28.4 |
| 1000 | 464 | 3177 | 83.4 / 100.1 | 739 | 16 | 76.0 | 28.8 |

How to read this:

- **Frame gap** is the time between `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks while a
  node is being dragged. 16.7 ms means 60 fps.
- **Drag time** includes Playwright's round-trip for each synthetic pointer
  move, so only compare it across rows, not with real-world feel.
- **Memory** excludes the WebView2 browser and GPU processes, which are shared
  helper processes. JS heap is `performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize` and varies
  with garbage-collection timing; the 1000-node figure is lower than the
  500-node one for that reason.
- A second run gave the same picture: 100 and 500 nodes at 60 fps, and 1000
  nodes at a p95 of 67–83 ms.

## Results

- **R0 smoke test (100 nodes): passes.** The map opens in under 70 ms, and
  drag and zoom hold 60 fps.
- **500 nodes:** still 60 fps while dragging.
- **1000 nodes:** dragging drops to roughly 12–15 fps. This is the measured
  scaling bottleneck and has not been profiled yet. Candidates:
  - The MiniMap re-renders every node on each change.
  - The inspector subscribes to every node change through `useNodes`.
  - Per-edge `useInternalNode` subscriptions.

  Profile before changing anything (backlog item in `docs/FEATURE_MATRIX.md`).
- **Engine:** operations take well under 10 ms at every size, so it is not a
  bottleneck.
